review_notes:
I read the whole supplied file. It is machine-generated certificate data. It repeats one template across 16 namespaces (hm37_{0,1}_0_{2..7}), and each namespace has `chunk`, 96 `s*_*` boxes, `c*_*` lemmas, `s*_eq`, `sums`, `sums_eq`, `checked`, `contains`, `atomChecked`, `atomContains`, `realChecked` and `realContains`.

The file has no `@[simp]` attributes, simp sets or simp lemmas to evaluate. The only simp use is `simp_rw [sums_eq]` inside each `checked`. It rewrites `chunk j i` to `sums j i`, where `sums` is a plain definition built from the `![s0,…,s5]` tables. The right-hand side does not mention `chunk`, so I see no rewrite cycle, no competing rules and no unwanted expansion. Using a local rewrite there seems appropriate, and a global simp attribute on `sums_eq` would not be justified. The other proofs use `decide +kernel`, `fin_cases`, `rw [← …]`, `exact` and `norm_num` on side goals, none of which depends on a simp interface.

I did not open the imported files. Any simp-lemma issue for `finSum`, `CBox` or `Contains` would belong to those files, not to this one. I found no justified finding under this rubric.
